title: Multi-Sensor Data Fusion for Enhanced Detection of Laser Fault Injection Attacks in Cryptographic Hardware: Practical Results
problem: Detecting laser fault injection attacks on cryptographic hardware deployed in FPGAs. Laser attacks offer high precision and temporal control, making them difficult to detect with single sensors.
motivation: Cryptographic hardware vulnerable to laser-based fault injection attacks; practical low-cost detection mechanism needed for security-critical deployments.
method: The detection system uses cheap sensors called Time-to-Digital Converters (TDCs) that measure the voltage changes caused by laser heating of the chip. By combining data from at least two of these sensors instead of just one (multi-sensor fusion), the system can reliably detect laser attacks while avoiding false alarms.
key_novelty: The key idea is combining measurements from multiple Time-to-Digital Converters (sensors that measure voltage timing) to reliably detect laser attacks on cryptographic chips with minimal false alarms.
contributions: Multi-sensor fusion scheme for reliable detection
Practical validation on Xilinx Artix-7 FPGA with real laser setup
limitations: Validation limited to AES implementation on Artix-7; generalization to other cryptographic algorithms and FPGA families not discussed.
